sections.content: How many people are "bakers and flour confectioners"?

27,070 people

were counted on the census as "bakers and flour confectioners" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Bakers and flour confectioners prepare and bake dough, pastry and cake mixtures and make and finish flour confectionary products by hand.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "bakers and flour confectioners" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 35 to 39 years. Of the whole working population 11.5% were aged 35 to 39 years. For people working as "bakers and flour confectioners", 13% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "bakers and flour confectioners" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "bakers and flour confectioners" included:

  • floorers and wall tilers
  • food, drink and tobacco process operatives
  • vehicle paint technicians

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "bakers and flour confectioners" there were a similar number of men and women (47.2% compared with 52.8%).

This means "bakers and flour confectioners" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "textiles, printing and other skilled trades".

Men made up 47.2% and women made up 52.8% of "bakers and flour confectioners"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "bakers and flour confectioners" included:

  • social and humanities scientists
  • laboratory technicians
  • packers, bottlers, canners and fillers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "bakers and flour confectioners" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "bakers and flour confectioners" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "bakers and flour confectioners", 11.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (58.5% compared with 41.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (72.9%) than self-employed (27.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cornwall, this is in the region of the South West.
